question: A reduction of 20% in the price of bananas enables a customer to buy 6 more bananas for ₹80. What is the reduced price of bananas per dozen (in ₹)?
solution:
**Given:**

A reduction of 20% in the price of bananas enables a customer to buy 6 more bananas for ₹80

**Calculation:**

Let the C.P of each banana be x

Total number of bananas in ₹ 80 = 80/x

New price = x – x × (20/100)

⇒ (100 - 20)x/100

⇒ 80x/100 or 4x/5

New number of bananas in ₹80 = 80/(4x/5)

⇒ 80/(4x/5)

⇒ 100/x

⇒ (100/x) – (80/x) = 6 

⇒ 20/x = 6 

⇒ x = 20/6

New price of bananas = 20/6 × 4/5

⇒ 8/3

The reduced price of bananas per dozen = (8/3) × 12

⇒ 32

**∴ The reduced price of bananas per dozen (in ₹) is 32.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **

Let the original price of a banana be 5x, new price will be 4x(reduced by 20%)

Now, according to the question,

⇒ 80over 4x - 80over 5x = 6

⇒ {80 (5 - 4)}over 4 times 5 times x = 6

⇒ {80 (5 - 4)}over 20 times x = 6

⇒ 4over x = 6

⇒ x = 2over3

The new price of bananas is,

⇒ 4x = 4 ×2over3

The price per dozen is

⇒ 4 × 2over3 × 12 = 32
